title: Control Board Fault
shortDescription: The main control (ERC/glass-top control) has detected an internal fault.
fullDescription:
F1 is a generic electronic control fault on Maytag cooktops. It indicates the control board has failed a self-check.

Start with a power cycle; if F1 persists, the control board needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker for 5 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new main control board if fault returns.

whenToCallPro: If the cooktop is hardwired and you are not comfortable with 240V wiring.

faq.q: Can I cook in the meantime?
faq.a: No; safety circuits will prevent heating.

title: Keypad or Touch Panel Fault
shortDescription: A stuck key or damaged touch membrane was detected.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates a touch input has been reported as active for too long, or the touch panel is reporting invalid signals. Spilled liquid or a cracked glass touch area is a common cause.

Clean the touch area and inspect for moisture under the glass.

fixSteps.title: Clean and dry
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe touch surface with a lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI board
fixSteps.instruction: If F2 returns, replace touch interface.

faq.q: Why does spilled water cause this?
faq.a: It creates false touch signals on capacitive panels.

title: Element Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A burner temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
F3 indicates one of the burner/element temperature sensors is out of range. On radiant cooktops this is the limiter; on induction tops it is the element thermistor.

The affected burner will be disabled to prevent overheating.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker before opening cooktop.

fixSteps.title: Access sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop or remove bottom panel per model.

whenToCallPro: If multiple sensors are faulty, suggesting control board issues.

faq.a: Some models display F3 plus burner number; otherwise test each.

title: Shorted Relay
shortDescription: A burner relay on the control has shorted closed.
fullDescription:
F4 is triggered when the control detects an element is receiving power even when off, indicating a stuck/shorted relay on the main board. This is a safety concern because the burner could heat unexpectedly.

Disable the cooktop at the breaker until repaired.
whenToCallPro: Recommended due to safety implications of stuck relays.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag cooktop F4 stuck relay control board

faq.q: Can I cook carefully around it?
faq.a: No; leave the breaker off until fixed.

title: Cooling Fan Fault (Induction)
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not running properly.
fullDescription:
On induction cooktops, F5 indicates the fan that cools the induction electronics is not reporting proper RPM. To protect components, the cooktop will shut down.

Check for obstruction under the cooktop or a failed fan motor.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure intake under or beside cooktop is clear.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If code returns, install new internal fan.

whenToCallPro: If the cooktop must be removed from counter.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag induction cooktop F5 cooling fan

faq.a: Using the cooktop like this risks permanent electronics damage.

title: Line Frequency / Voltage Fault
shortDescription: Incoming line voltage is out of specification.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates the control detects abnormal line frequency (should be 60 Hz in North America) or voltage. Common during brownouts, generator operation, or bad connections.

Verify good power at the outlet/terminal block before assuming the cooktop is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Measure line voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 240V L1-L2 at the cooktop feed.

fixSteps.title: Tighten terminal block
fixSteps.instruction: With breaker off, check and tighten all supply lugs.

whenToCallPro: Any line-voltage troubleshooting if you are not experienced with 240V.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag cooktop F6 line voltage error

faq.a: Yes if it produces unstable frequency.

title: Communication Fault
shortDescription: Main control and UI board are not communicating.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates loss of serial communication between the main control and the touch/display board. Often caused by a disconnected ribbon cable or a failed board.

Reseat cables first; replace the failing board second.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open cooktop and reseat ribbon cables between boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace a board
fixSteps.instruction: If F7 persists, replace UI first, then main if needed.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not help and diagnosis is unclear.

faq.q: Why does a loose cable happen?
faq.a: Vibration or prior service can loosen connectors.

title: Induction Module Overtemperature
shortDescription: An induction power module has exceeded safe temperature.
fullDescription:
F8 on induction cooktops indicates the IGBT/power module is running too hot. Caused by airflow blockage, ambient overheat, or a failing module.

Allow the cooktop to cool, clear vents, and verify fan operation.

fixSteps.title: Clear airflow path
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the installation leaves required clearance under/around the cooktop.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If F8 persists, the induction module needs professional replacement.

whenToCallPro: Anything beyond clearing airflow on induction modules.

faq.a: Yes - heavy iron cookware can heat the glass more and raise module temps.

title: Pan Detection Error (Induction)
shortDescription: The cooktop cannot detect suitable cookware.
fullDescription:
F9 on induction cooktops means no ferromagnetic cookware is detected, or the pan is too small or off-center. Ensure induction-compatible cookware is used and placed correctly on the element.

A magnet should stick firmly to the pan base for induction use.

fixSteps.title: Check cookware
fixSteps.instruction: Use a magnet to verify pan is induction-compatible.

fixSteps.title: Center the pan
fixSteps.instruction: Place pan squarely over burner symbol, at least 4 inches diameter.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If compatible pan still fails, service needed.

whenToCallPro: Only if a known-good pan still triggers F9.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag induction cooktop F9 pan detection

faq.a: Only pans a magnet strongly sticks to.

title: Runaway Temperature
shortDescription: A burner is heating uncontrollably or sensor reports runaway.
fullDescription:
F10 is a safety fault indicating temperature rising faster than expected or above safe limits. The cooktop cuts power to affected circuits.

This is typically caused by a shorted element or failed sensor feedback. Do not attempt to continue cooking.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Diagnose element, sensor, and control; replace failed component.
